_description: Skin Classification Categories - Step 6 of the FaceMed AI Pipeline
description: The final Dense layer uses softmax activation to produce 5 probability scores that sum to 1.0. The class with the highest probability is the dominant skin condition.

classes.description: Characterized by inflammatory breakouts, blocked follicles, papules, and pustules. Caused by excess sebum, bacterial growth, and hormonal imbalance.
clinicalMarkers: Red circular spots with white/yellow centers
classes.keyPixelSignature: High R-channel spots on peach skin base

classes.description: Low skin hydration, compromised lipid barrier, visible flaking and scaling. Skin appears dull and rough to touch.
clinicalMarkers: Visible white flake particles on skin surface
classes.keyPixelSignature: Desaturated base with random bright flake speckles
classes.prevalence: Affects ~30% of adults; higher in cold/dry climates

classes.description: Overactive sebaceous glands produce excess oil. Skin appears shiny and reflective, especially in the T-zone.
clinicalMarkers: Glossy specular reflections on forehead and nose
classes.keyPixelSignature: Bright white reflection blobs on T-zone regions
classes.prevalence: Affects ~40% of adults; more common in humid climates

classes.description: Healthy, balanced skin with adequate hydration and minimal visible concerns. Pores are small and skin tone is even.
clinicalMarkers: No visible excess oil or flaking
classes.keyPixelSignature: Uniform peach skin tone with minimal variation

classes.description: Uneven melanin distribution causing dark spots, patches, and uneven skin tone. Caused by UV exposure, hormonal changes, or post-inflammatory response.
clinicalMarkers: Uneven skin tone across face regions
classes.keyPixelSignature: Dark elliptical patches with all RGB channels depressed
classes.prevalence: Affects ~70% of pregnant women; up to 20% of general population

exampleOutput.interpretation: Highest score is acne (0.87 = 87%). Primary condition: Acne Vulgaris. Secondary concern: Oily Skin (72%).
